title: Prime-to-ell profinite linear monodromy has finite image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $H$ be a profinite group all of whose finite continuous quotient groups have order prime to $\ell$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space and let $\rho:H\to\operatorname{GL}_E(M)$ be a representation such that $H\times M\to M$ is continuous. Then $\rho(H)$ is finite and has order prime to $\ell$. The zero-dimensional vector space is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, pp. 2-3, stable lattice argument; agent corollary using the filtration of the principal congruence subgroup by additive residue-field matrices.

proof.text: Use the assumed equality of the topology of E with its spectral-norm topology, and eq_moduleTopology to replace the topology of M by moduleTopology E M. Apply [lem-sfb-stable-lattice-finite-matrix-reductions] to the compact group H, the vector space M, and the jointly continuous action. Obtain the stable lattice, its integer basis and field basis e, integral representation A, and finite continuous positive-level reductions B_n. The construction includes rank zero, so no separate zero-dimensional case is needed.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3; agent prime-to-ell corollary, assembly of the two extracted arguments.

proof.text: The kernel of B_n is the inverse image of the open singleton identity in its discrete target. Package it as an open normal subgroup N_n of H. The first isomorphism theorem identifies H/N_n with the range of B_n, so the hypothesis on all open normal quotients gives coprimality of its order with ell. Apply [lem-sfb-coprime-congruence-kernel-rigidity] using the finite positive-level images and these coprimality statements; at level one it gives ker B_1 = ker A.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3; agent prime-to-ell corollary, assembly of the two extracted arguments.

proof.text: If g belongs to ker B_1, rigidity gives A(g)=1. The coordinate formula in the field basis e then gives rho(g)(e_j)=e_j for every j; basis extensionality yields rho(g)=1. Thus ker B_1 is contained in ker rho. A subgroup containing an open subgroup is open, so ker rho is open. Package ker rho as an open normal subgroup N of H. Its quotient is finite because H is compact, and its order is coprime to ell by the hypothesis. The first isomorphism theorem H/ker rho = rho(H) transfers both conclusions. Empty-basis extensionality covers rank zero.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3; agent prime-to-ell corollary, assembly of the two extracted arguments.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3 for the stable lattice; agent congruence-kernel corollary and V6 Lean assembly via the open representation kernel.
